articles.title: SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite Review - IGN
articles.body:
By some accounts, SteelSeries invented the concept of a high-end gaming headset with its $329 Arctis Pro Wireless and $349 Arctis Nova Pro Wireless headsets. And indeed, we've seen a long list of other gaming brands follow its lead in offering premium headsets with features like active noise cancellation, multi-device base stations and deep software customization.

Now, SteelSeries is back with an even higher-end model, the $600 Arctis Nova Elite. It comes with redesigned carbon fiber drivers, a more capable four-source base station and hi-res wireless audio certification, but is any gaming headset worth that high a price? After a month of testing, I’m starting to think that the heretofore dormant ultra-premium category might be about to spring into life.

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite – Design and Features

At first glance, the Nova Elite looks very similar to the Arctis Nova Pro Wireless released in 2023 – though the classy sage/gold and obsidian colorways at least hint to the upgrades within. The comfortable fabric suspension headband returns intact, with stainless steel and aluminum used throughout the frame to provide a convincingly durable design. The volume wheel has transformed from plastic in the prior models to metal too, with audible steps that provide good feedback to signify the increments in volume change. The memory foam ear cushions complete the headset, providing moderate levels of passive noise cancellation.

Though its gaming origins are unmistakable, this is one of the nicest-looking headsets I've ever tested and it doesn't look garishly out of place next to similarly-priced lifestyle headphones. The black obsidian model is particularly adept at not drawing attention, though its shiny metal accents again attest to a high-end design.

Inside, the 40mm dynamic drivers used in the prior Arctis Nova Pro models have been upgraded to two-piece carbon fiber models, wrapped in a brass surround. SteelSeries says that the new "pistonic" design moves up and down without jitter to avoid distortion, and can reproduce sounds from 10Hz to 40KHz.

The headset makes the most of these internal upgrades too, with 96KHz/24-bit Hi-Res audio over 2.4GHz wireless or the LC3+ Bluetooth codec. The Nova Elite also sports more effective ANC than its predecessor, while the microphone uses a 32KHz/16-bit wide-band connection. If you retract the default microphone, as you might while on-the-go, a new backup beam-forming mic is used instead.

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite – Setup and Connectivity

The GameHub base station also sees new ornamentation – with a gold volume wheel on the sage/gold colorway – which is again backed with new functionality. The two USB inputs on the original Arctis Nova Pro Wireless have been upgraded to three, allowing for full-fat digital connections to a PC, PS5, and Xbox for example. And unlike the older Nova Pro model, now two of these connections can be live at once, with the game station automatically selecting the correct inputs based on activity. It’s worth noting that there’s only one version of the Arctis Nova Elite, with the third USB-C input optionally enabling support for Xbox’s proprietary wireless standard, rather than requiring the purchase of an Xbox-specific variant as we’ve seen on past Arctis headsets.

A further fourth 3.5mm input allows for an additional connection, while the headset itself can also maintain a simultaneous Bluetooth connection, with a dedicated on/off button.

Getting set up is extremely straightforward, as it's just a case of running one of the provided USB-C or 3.5mm cables to the source of your choice, or alternatively pairing over Bluetooth.

Once connected, you can long press the back button on the GameHub to change between various display modes, which show the volume level of each source, their equaliser settings, or the current bit-rate and left/right channel levels. Additionally, track data from Tidal is also shown when it is playing, though I wish this extended to all common media players like Spotify or YouTube Music.

Long pressing the volume wheel enters a menu, allowing you to set the third USB input to Xbox or regular mode; change equalizer, gain, noise control, and microphone settings; swap between wireless and Bluetooth; change line out settings; or change system settings like microphone brightness, display brightness, or power-saving modes. It's very much the same system as the Arctis Nova Pro Wireless, with a few extra options that don't feel too overwhelming.

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite – Battery Life

The base station also maintains the excellent swappable battery system that's become the trademark of Arctis Pro Wireless headsets, with each battery promising 30 hours of play time. While one battery is being run down inside the headset, the other charges up inside the base station, so you're never left in the lurch.

The switchover is still a little awkward – you need to physically swap in the next battery within five seconds after the first is removed in order for the headset to automatically power itself on again – but it's something that you'll quickly adjust to as an Arctis Nova Elite owner. (The only way to prevent this would be to include a battery or supercapacitor inside the headset itself, which would likely add significant cost and complexity to the design, so it's an understandable restriction.)

In situations where you're without the base station, such as international travel, you can also use a regular USB-C charger to top up the battery. This isn't ideal ergonomically, with the cable coming out of one earcup at a right angle, but I think it's unlikely to be a common occurrence for most users. SteelSeries claims that a 15-minute charging session is sufficient for four hours of usage, so you don't need to top up for long in order to get a decent charge on the headset once again.

In my testing, the Nova Elite managed to keep closely to its 30-hour estimate, and given the ease of swapping to a fresh battery, I never ran into any difficulties. Even on a single battery, I was able to use the headset for a full week of gaming and music listening, averaging four or five hours a day.

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite – Software

Aside from its hi-res audio certification, the Arctis Elite offers largely the same PC software experience as its predecessors, complete with a multi-tiered GG app that contains sections for more basic adjustments (Engine), powerful audio programming (Sonar) and additional settings (Moments, 3D Aim Trainer, Giveaways, News). Sonar is incredibly capable, with a parametric EQ and a long list of game-specific equaliser presets, including some created in collaboration with esports teams.

That said, its insistence on creating many additional audio devices can be bothersome if you tend to manually select your desired audio device in Windows, for example. Ideally, you'd want to run everything through the GameHub and SteelSeries' Sonar software, rather than having separate speakers or microphones controlled in different apps, but that may not be practical for some setups.

What's new for the Arctis Elite is the addition of the Arctis mobile app, which was introduced with the Arctis Nova 5 and has been a feature of each additional SteelSeries headset released since. Given the multi-device nature of the Arctis Elite – which ought to see it being used as your everyday Bluetooth headset, your PC gaming headset, and your console headset of choice – having an app to select presets and make other changes quickly is a game-changer. There's still no way to create or modify these presets on the mobile app, but given the huge number of available options, this isn't a terrifically troublesome restriction.

Finally, the full gamut of virtual surround sound modes are supported on each platform – Dolby Atmos and Windows Sonic on PC and Xbox, and Tempest 3D Audio on PS5 – though I preferred to use the headset in stereo mode in faster and more competitive games like Counter-Strike 2, Valorant, and Battlefield 2042.

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite – Performance and Gaming

The Arctis Nova Pro Wireless was already an excellent performer when it came to gaming, with its 40mm dynamic drivers providing excellent spatial cues, plenty of detail, and a relatively neutral sound signature out of the box that's easy to listen to for extended periods. The Arctis Nova Elite sounds even better, thanks to its carbon fiber drivers and brass surrounds, making individual sounds a touch easier to distinguish in a crowded soundscape.

Compared to the only other extremely high-end headset I have, the $900 Audeze LCD-GX with its titanic 106mm planar magnetic drivers, the Nova Elite is surprisingly similar while being substantially cheaper, wireless instead of wired, and much more comfortable to wear due to its lighter weight. The inclusion of ANC is also a godsend for louder environments, whether you're trying to clutch in Counter-Strike or just relax with some music on a crowded train.

The Nova Elite's wireless hi-res certification is also intriguing, although as always the issue is that true high-res audio is extremely hard to find outside of a few services like Tidal, and practically unknown in games. I did subscribe to Tidal for the purposes of this review, and found a few small improvements in back-to-back listening sessions with hi-res audio enabled (requiring a settings change in Windows to 24-bit 96KHz) and more standard 16-bit 44.1KHz playback. I wouldn't say that most people ought to care deeply about hi-res audio, especially in the gaming arena, but it is nice to know that the Arctis Nova Elite isn't likely to be the limiting factor here.

The Arctis Nova Elite's microphone also shows a modest improvement, though as usual wired headsets and dedicated USB or XLR microphones will still offer the best quality for more serious use.

Ultimately, there are sure to be audiophile headphones that sound better than the Arctis Nova Elite, but delivering this level of audio quality alongside a full-fat gaming feature list is unheard of – only Audeze's significantly heavier and bulkier planar magnetic headsets come close in my experience.

articles.title: GTA 6 Fans Celebrate as Cyberleek Cryptocurrency Crashes Hard
articles.summary: GTA 6 fans are celebrating after the Cyberleek memecoin crashed hard yesterday, scuppering the leaker’s crypto scheme.
articles.body:
GTA 6 fans are celebrating after the Cyberleek memecoin crashed hard yesterday, scuppering the leaker’s crypto scheme.

Cyberleek had tied various types of GTA 6 gameplay leaks to the Cyberleek market cap, ranging from $5 million to $25 million. The leaker also threatened to release a build of the game — supposedly over 200 GB in size — if the memecoin hit a $30 million market cap.

Already this week a number of gameplay clips were reportedly leaked after market cap goals were hit, including gameplay that allegedly shows Lucia fully naked, and, more recently, the alleged leak of a “Lucia closeup 4k” video.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

Cyberleek has threatened to release a new unauthorized GTA 6 gameplay video every day, assuming the memecoin market cap targets were met, and launched yet another gameplay poll designed to encourage spending on the memecoin.

However, the Cyberleek memecoin has crashed, with a current market cap of $1.7 million, down from a high of $7.8 million on October 11. It is now highly unlikely to hit that $30 million target, and may struggle to hit the other targets Cyberleek had set for further leaks.

Of course, Cyberleek may ignore the targets and just release gameplay anyway. But the bigger question is whether Cyberleek really does have a build of GTA 6, and, if so, would actually release it. Assuming Cyberleek has a working build, releasing it into the wild would be catastrophic for Rockstar and parent company Take-Two, as it would no-doubt spark a frenzy of AI-powered projects that would threaten the potential success of GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S when it comes out next month.

For now, GTA 6 fans are celebrating the Cyberleek crash. “Whoever is dropping money on this deserves to lose their money lol. You are begging to get scammed,” one person said. “There is a god,” another added. “Anyone who gave this moron cash deserved this. What the hell did people expect?” another commented.

Fans had spent the last week calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and is likely to do so again ahead of GTA 6’s official release date, if they haven’t already. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000.

Yesterday, IGN reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked . A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggests access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to that in any way, which suggests this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats and won’t be possible in the official release.

One theory is that Cyberleak was able to access this state for both Lucia and Jason because in at least one mission players will see both characters naked, perhaps in a nudist resort. As it stands, this is all speculation, and it is unknown if GTA 6 will feature either character naked at any point — officially at least.

Cyberleek has threatened Rockstar and parent company Take-Two with the release of a full playthrough of the game’s story if they fail to release GTA 6 on-disc and issue a public apology — and, as we’ve explained, the market cap of the memecoin hits $30 million. Of course, few believe these GTA 6 leaks are about campaigning for physical media — rather they're about making money from a crypto scam.

"Here's the deal, nice and clean," Cyberleek's threat began. "CYBERLEEK hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out — full story mode, played to the end, credits and all. Don't believe it has full story mode? Ask for what you want to see, and it gets provided. Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology. They can take it at any moment. Or they can gamble that CL is bluffing. Everyone knows which one they'll pick."

Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Take-Two. The company issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. But Cyberleek reemerged last week with the release of a 24-minute GTA 6 gameplay video that reportedly showed cutscenes, story beats, playable characters Jason and Lucia naked (in the case of Jason, full-frontal nudity), and a first-person camera.

It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. Recent developments suggest Cyberleek remains at large and defiant in the face of potential legal action.

In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks , describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima Wears Joy Division T-Shirt to Sony Visit, Sparking Johnny Silverhand Arasaka Tower Comparison
articles.summary: Hideo Kojima posted pictures on social media of himself visiting Sony in Japan while wearing a Joy Division T-shirt — and fans are certainly getting plenty of joy out of it.
articles.body:
Hideo Kojima posted pictures on social media of himself visiting Sony in Japan while wearing a Joy Division T-shirt — and fans are certainly getting plenty of joy out of it.

The Metal Gear creator took to social media to post the photos showing him standing outside Sony City, also known as the Sony Corporate Office Building, in Tokyo, Japan. That wouldn’t normally be anything to write home about, but given recent events, there’s plenty of context we need to run through.

Earlier this year, Sony ditched Physint , Kojima’s Metal Gear spiritual successor, leaving the legendary game developer scrambling to find another publisher for the project. In an interview with IGN , Kojima revealed how he feared for the future of Kojima Productions after Sony confirmed its decision via a Zoom call.

Visited Sony City. — HIDEO_KOJIMA (@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN) October 13, 2026

Kojima pitched Physint to Microsoft and new gaming boss Asha Sharma, who were suitably impressed to snap up the cast adrift project, including its adaptation rights for film and TV. In the wake of Physint’s move to Xbox, Bloomberg reported that Sony had concerns around the success of Kojima’s Death Stranding, as well as Physint’s development timeline, budget, and platform strategy. Kojima Productions issued a statement in response, although it failed to directly address Bloomberg’s reporting.

“Make no mistake, this was a serious situation for the studio with a range of potentially significant implications,” Kojima Productions said. “While we recognise that the article may have caused alarm, we want to reassure you all, for the record: that the studio is in a healthy, profitable state, development for Physint continues to move forward with Xbox, and our relationship with PlayStation remains strong.​”

In our interview, Kojima insisted there was no bad blood with Sony, saying: “... from my side, I love Sony. And I don't have any bad feelings against them because I know that it's a tough time in the game industry. I've been working with them for like 30 years… Mr. Ken Kutaragi, Mr. Hirai, I was close with them. But it's not like that recently. I realized that, okay, this is the reality. It's the 10th anniversary of my studio. My studio might collapse, right?”

Kojima added that Sony did not provide a reason for canceling Physint, nor had it contacted him since the decision was made. “But I'm not fighting with Sony,” he continued. “We're not in a dispute. But what I want to say is that we've been together for 30 years and we have this relationship. So if this was the conclusion, I would've wanted to hear it a little earlier. But that meeting in June, they just gave us the final notice.

“As I said, my mind went blank, so I didn't really ask a lot of questions. It was more like, what should I do with my company? So that was what was on my mind at the time. I've always been a big Sony fan. I've been using a Walkman. All my cameras are Sony. So I have no bad feelings towards them.”

Fast forward four months, and we have Kojima visiting Sony. What should we make of this? Are the pair working on a secret project together? Could there be more to come from Death Stranding? Or is this… nothing? Either way, fans are having their fun, with people picking up on Kojima’s decision to wear a T-shirt for a band called Joy Division, and comparing the situation to Johnny Silverhand's ill-fated and destructive assault on Arasaka Tower in Cyberpunk 2077.

@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN — Bucky | Palworld (@Bucky_cm) October 13, 2026

@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN — Sköma (@HoloSkma) October 13, 2026

@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN @Kojima_Hideo — elián 🍊 (@elianrepatriate) October 13, 2026

After the Physint news broke, there has been intense speculation about the budget for the game. In a recent New York Times profile of Asha Sharma, it was reported that Xbox may have negotiated a deal for less than you’d expect for a full price, triple-A spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid from the creator of the franchise.

Kojima told IGN that Microsoft was “not thinking of just funding a game. They're thinking about movies and anime. It's more about the IP. Let's create a new IP. And that's bigger in scale, so to speak. And not many other game publishers or game developers have that kind of vision.”

Physint remains without a release window. It is expected after the launch of OD, Kojima's next video game for Xbox.

Photo by Phillip Faraone/Getty Images for Kojima Productions.

articles.title: Planet Zoo 2 Is a Vibrant and Thriving Sequel Full of Lovely Visual Upgrades Excitingly Expanded Zookeeping Mechanics - Review
articles.summary: A vibrant and thriving sequel full of lovely visual upgrades and expanded mechanics.
articles.body:
Running my dream menagerie in Planet Zoo is always going to feel a little different than the entertainment-focused spectacles of Planet Coaster or fantastical dino parks of Jurassic World Evolution. All of these gorgeous beasts and birds are real species we share the planet with and, in some cases, have put on the endangered list. So I was glad to see that Frontier's sequel put an even deeper emphasis on conservation as a main goal this time around, even if certain pieces of that – like wildlife reserves – feel a bit less fleshed-out than they could be.

When it comes to the daily tasks of building enclosures, hiring staff, and caring for animals, there isn't a ton that has changed since the original Planet Zoo . In that way, it feels more like a gentle evolution than a wildly ambitious one. And that's not necessarily a bad thing. If you played the first game, you should have no trouble getting your bearings in this one. There are a lot more options for adding detail, but building a functional zoo doesn't require you to learn all of them.

The species list is downright impressive, too, with over 130 creatures of all sizes to display. Some of these are exhibit-based, meaning they live in a smaller terrarium and don't have all of the same features of the bigger ones. And only around half of the list is eligible to eventually be released into the wild – more on that later. But at no point did the roster ever feel stingy. I even learned about a new species of horse!

The addition of aviaries and aquariums is the first big, shiny, new feature that isn't purely visual. And the flexibility allowed by this system is impressive. Whereas in the Jurassic World Evolution games, creating habitats for swimmers and flyers was a matter of snapping large, modular pieces together, Planet Zoo 2 gives you a lot of fine control over the shape, look, and in the case of aquariums, even depth of an exhibit.

I was really excited when I realized you can build glass tunnels through an aquarium exhibit. You can even build your entire zoo this way, as long as you stick to species that can share the same watery home without issue. Some species will fight or try to eat each other if placed together, just like in the first Planet Zoo. But there are also aquatic and semi-aquatic creatures who have different needs in terms of water temperature and salinity. If you want freshwater and saltwater exhibits in the same zoo, you even need two different filtration networks, which was an extra level of planning and realism that I enjoyed.

That brings me to the major advantage that sets Planet Zoo 2 apart from its coaster- and dino-based sister games: it's actually a challenging economic simulation. Of course, in the sandbox mode, you can turn off just about anything you don't want to deal with – from staff happiness to animal aging to the very concept of money. But as someone who very much feels that the difficulty of keeping the lights on is part of the experience, I was thrilled to find that task is not completely trivial.

If you check out my review of Planet Coaster 2, you'll recall I was deflated by the fact that I could put down one flat ride and a couple vending machines, walk away from my PC, and come back to find I had made essentially unlimited money from my sad little park. I tried a similar experiment in Planet Zoo 2, making one small exhibit with only warthogs to start and gouging my guests as much as possible to make a profit. It didn't work. And that's great! Between six different types of staff members to manage, complex guest and animal needs, and the fact that visitors can be very realistically prickly about ticket prices if they don't think they're getting their money's worth, Planet Zoo 2 has a lot to chew on even before you start moving into the rich breeding and conservation systems. There are still a couple pieces of the management screen that felt a little underbaked. Your Sustainability rating is just based on which types of power generators and wastebins you install, which is a trivial choice with no major downsides that I never really thought about again after achieving five stars before the gates even opened. But the other components of building my zoo's reputation really gave me something to strive for.

The possibilities for customization have also expanded quite a bit in that nearly all buildings now have fully-modeled interiors that guests and staff can interact with. You can design your perfect break room inside and out, and even tweak the kitchens where the animals' meals are prepared. This system goes even deeper with new, modular gift shops and restaurants in which functional seating areas and shelf displays can be placed that actually affect dining capacity and items available for purchase. I'm an absolute amateur at using these powerful tools to their greatest potential. But since the Steam Workshop once again lets me download little decorations or even whole buildings from far more talented and dedicated detailers, I can still benefit from their versatility.

There's also a campaign that serves mostly as a kind of extended tutorial. It's fine. I mainly used it as inspiration for what kinds of things I could build with the new tools. The characters still talk kind of like they're on a BBC children's program, but they're a bit less outwardly goofy this time around, which meant I had a bit more patience for them. And there is kind of a plot, even, revolving around exposing the crimes of a major corporation claiming to be environmentally friendly while actually putting fragile ecosystems at risk. It does the job well enough.

The other substantial new element of Planet Zoo 2 comes in the form of wildlife reserves, which are completely separate maps on which you paint biomes instead of enclosures, then increase their rating by introducing appropriate plants and re-wilding a variety of native species. While it can be a lot of fun to drive around in my little cart and take pictures of my zoo's former residents back in their natural habitat, the management side of these reserves feels a little shallow.

There are tons of tags for different kinds of animals that can occupy necessary biological niches on your preserves, but establishing and maintaining ecosystems wasn't always quite so satisfying. Getting rid of invasive plants, for instance, is just a matter of clicking on them with the bulldozer tool. There's no need to hire rangers or botanists to maintain the land. You're doing it all with godlike powers. I will say, I do really like the new nature brushes, which can be used to paint a variety of different canopy and understory plants with one tool. You can even make your own!

The water tools don't hold up to the same standard. There's a lot of customization in terms of surface texture, color, opacity, and so forth. But every body of water is ultimately still a fixed height, and has to be placed in a trough. It's not really possible to make something like a convincing river that flows downhill without resorting to some clever special effects that require a lot of tweaking. It made me miss the dynamic waterfalls from Jurassic World Evolution 3.

Still, it's great to have a physical place I can go visit when an animal's time at my zoo is done. I can even snap pictures of them to earn Conservation Credits, Planet Zoo 2's secondary currency that is required to adopt certain higher-tier endangered animals. I also enjoyed being able to invest my zoo's resources into new conservation projects, which offer a helpful and reliable way to turn money into Conservation Credits if you don't have any animals currently ready for release.

articles.title: Ben Affleck Warns Against Celebrating Box Office Failure of Tom Cruise's Digger, Says It Could Discourage Risk-Taking in Hollywood
articles.summary: Ben Affleck has compared the reaction to Tom Cruise’s Digger to “high-school bullying,” insisting the eagerness with which some have celebrated its box office failure could discourage risk-taking in Hollywood.
articles.body:
Ben Affleck has compared the reaction to Tom Cruise’s Digger to “high-school bullying,” insisting the eagerness with which some have celebrated its box office failure could discourage risk-taking in Hollywood.

Digger is reportedly set to lose an eye-watering $250 million by the end of its theatrical run , with Warner Bros. expecting it to cap at around $40 million globally. Its opening weekend brought in just $8 million domestically and $12 million internationally. It's currently on $35.3 million globally after two weekends in theaters. Variety reported that Digger may go down one of the biggest Hollywood flops of all time.

Directed by back-to-back Best Director Oscar winner Alejandro G. Iñárritu (Birdman, The Revenant), and starring screen legend Tom Cruise, Digger has split both critics and audiences. Attempts have been made to weaponise the mixed reaction in its favour, and Hollywood stars have come out in its defence, but Digger does not appear to have the legs to recover from its initial box office disaster status.

Speaking on Josh Horowitz's Happy Sad Confused podcast , Batman star Ben Affleck defended ambitious filmmaking and risk-taking, issuing a warning that the reaction to Digger could see Hollywood retreat into safer bets such as sequels and recognizable IP adaptations.

"It's a little bit like the high-school bullying thing,” Affleck argued, “with people who hadn’t even seen movies. You see it happening now, frankly, with Digger. Everybody wants to celebrate this bomb as if it’s the most exciting thing to happen. And you think like, it’s a pretty ambitious, interesting movie made by interesting people who have talent.

“Everybody wants to count the money, what it lost or whatever. To me, I just think, if you punish movies that take risks, guess what you're going to get? A bunch of s**tty homogenized movies. You cannot do something interesting without taking a big swing. And that means you're going to sometimes look bad."

Digger has a 53% rating on Rotten Tomatoes' Tomatometer , and a more positive 74% user review rating on its Popcornmeter. IGN’s Digger review returned a 6/10. We said: “Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs.”

Digger trolled the negative reviews in its most recent ad campaign, but that failed to move the needle. Tom Cruise himself has yet to issue an official statement in response.

articles.title: Dan Houser Reveals How 9/11 Changed GTA Forever
articles.summary: 25 years later, Dan Houser recalls how GTA’s iconic cover art style only exists because of 9/11.
articles.body:
There’s arguably no more recognisable style of cover art than that of the Grand Theft Auto series. The panelled collection of images featuring characters and locations from each open world that has adorned each game box from 2001’s GTA 3 to the upcoming GTA 6 is etched into each of our minds. It all nearly looked completely different, though.

We spoke to Dan Houser, former VP at Rockstar and writer of almost all of the studio’s games from 1999 until 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, as part of our IGN30 Icons Series. When reminiscing about the developer’s most famous series, Grand Theft Auto, Houser shared how it felt to see elements of his creation permeate into the real world.

“GTA has become part of the wider cultural fabric,” he said. “I mean, you sort of saw that on YouTube clips and whatever else that would have the HUD on it, and people using the logo and things like that. When you go to any big tourist resort, you'll have a sort of GTA cover art-inspired T-shirt available. So you began to see that creep in 10 years ago, so I suppose.”

The bold, colourful style of that cover art came out of tragedy, though, as Houser revealed that the original look for GTA 3’s box had to be changed at the last minute due to the New York terror attack on September 11, 2011.

“What's funny is the cover art that became the iconic GTA cover art; Stephen Bliss did that in about two evenings because the old cover art was probably being too offensive to release after 9/11 because they were burning buildings in it,” Houser revealed. “So it would've been fine if there hadn't just been 9/11. So that look of the shards, the squares that became very iconic, only appeared because of 9/11.”

These changes, as well as some involving the actual content of the game, meant a slight delay for GTA 3 from its originally planned release date of October 3, 2001 to October 22. Though only a few weeks, it piled on the pressure for Rockstar and Houser, who were by no means sure it would become the landmark success it eventually did.

“So I remember in early 2001, Take-Two was on the point of economic failure at the time,” Houser recalled. “We were struggling to get the game done, but we thought the game was going to be amazing and took it to E3 on the show floor and nobody cared about it. So that was dispiriting up to a point. And then the game came out six, seven months later. And that was just after 9/11.”

GTA 3, of course, takes place in Liberty City, a fictionalised version of New York City, so you can see why a change in approach was needed. “There were a couple of bits of content that would've been fine, but in the exact aftermath of 9/11, were maybe a little bit too much,” Houser explained. “So we had to take those out, and the team will rally round and remove those and edit a couple of lines of dialogue and did a quick content stand and thought it was fine. And then the game came out in October of 2001. It kind of was a gradual all the way through till Christmas 2001 into early 2002, and it just didn't stop selling. It's not like any single week was that massive. It was that every week it just rumbled on.”

Some of these tweaks were detailed by Houser in a 2011 interview with Edge magazine. "As far as I recall, we changed the colour of the cop cars so they weren't identical to NYPD, we altered the flight path of a plane so that it didn't look like it was flying into or behind a skyscraper, and we removed one mission as it made a reference to terrorists,” he said at the time.

The first 3D Grand Theft Auto wasn’t the only piece of media that had to make alterations in the wake of the terror attacks. Other video games, such as EA’s Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2, had to redesign its packaging , and Hideo Kojima’s Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty had sections involving the destruction of parts of Manhattan and the Statue of Liberty removed .

Other cases include the trailer for Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man having to be recut to remove a helicopter being caught in a giant web between the World Trade Center towers. Men in Black 2 underwent huge reshoots for similar reasons, and planned sequels to both True Lies and Forrest Gump were cancelled.

25 years on, the same template for GTA game covers is still being used. You can check out all of the details we picked out from GTA 6’s art reveal here . For more on GTA 6, you can read our full interview with Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson , how the game will tackle the current political climate , and why Dan Houser says he won’t be playing it .

articles.title: GTA 6 Reportedly Set for PC Q1 2027
articles.summary: GTA 6 will launch on PC just a few months after consoles, according to a new report.
articles.body:
Rockstar reportedly plans to release GTA 6 on PC during the first quarter of 2027.

GamesBeat reported the news based on four sources who asked to remain anonymous. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two are yet to comment.

If true, it would mean GTA 6 hitting PC just a few months after it launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026. Some had anticipated a longer wait for the game on PC, given it took nearly two years for GTA 5 to launch on PC after consoles.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

The PC launch may tie into the release of GTA 6's multiplayer mode, which fans are calling GTA Online 2 while they wait for official word from Rockstar. While Rockstar has yet to confirm an online mode for GTA 6, last month Twitch boss Dan Clancy said GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called — will launch next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick has always responded with vague comments when asked about the prospect of launching GTA 6 on PC, pointing to Rockstar for announcements. In May, Zelnick told Bloomberg that Rockstar "always starts on console because I think with regard to a release like that you're judged by serving the core. Like really serving the core consumer. If your core consumer isn't there, if they're not served first and best, you kind of don't hit your other consumers.”

Red Dead Redemption, GTA 5, LA Noire, Max Payne 3, and Red Dead Redemption 2 all came to PC after consoles. And while GTA's core audience may be on console, it has a huge fanbase of active players on PC, fueled by GTA Online and role-play servers.

Indeed, 12 months ago, Zelnick said the industry was “moving towards PC,” telling CNBC’s Squawk Box that the video game business was trending towards “open rather than closed.”

Assuming GTA 6 does come to PC early next year, one of the big questions players will have is how it runs compared to on consoles. Rockstar has yet to confirm the performance of GTA 6 on consoles, so we're still in the dark when it comes to frames-per-second and resolution. But the expectation is that any PC version would be capable of better performance, assuming your rig is powerful enough.

articles.title: Nvidia RTX 5090 Reportedly Dead, but It's So Expensive That It Doesn't Really Matter
articles.summary: While the RTX 5090 was already hard enough to get at a reasonable price, new leaks suggest that Nvidia is flat-out discontinuing its flagship graphics card.
articles.body:
While the RTX 5090 was already hard enough to get at a reasonable price, new leaks suggest that Nvidia is flat-out discontinuing its flagship graphics card.

GPU leaker zed__wang on X/Twitter posted about the RTX 5090, saying there would be "no more GB202 for 5090, confirmed." They then followed up with a quote tweet, saying, "All future GB202 supplies are RTX Pro exclusive."

For the uninitiated, GB202 is the name of the actual GPU die that powers the RTX 5090, and it has always powered more than just the RTX 5090. Instead, the GB202 powers nine distinct workstation and data center GPUs, according to TechPowerUp . It shouldn't be too surprising, then, that Nvidia would opt to prioritize much more expensive graphics cards like the Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell, which costs around $18,000, rather than the RTX 5090, which costs around $9,000 on Newegg these days.

Nvidia also hasn't been shy about prioritizing AI over the gaming division, with the company dropping gaming from its earnings report , and working it into the 'Edge Computing' category.

While the leak suggests that the discontinuation of the RTX 5090 is confirmed, it is anything but. Nvidia hasn't commented on its flagship card going away. That doesn't mean much on the surface, but if you look back to February, similar rumors were spinning up about the RTX 5070 Ti , and no matter how convincing those leaks were, they ended up being completely false.

I've asked Nvidia for comment and will update this article if I hear back, but I suspect that this RTX 5090 situation is very similar. Back then, production on the RTX 5070 Ti stalled as VRAM was being prioritized for data centers, but the RTX 5070 Ti itself didn't get discontinued. It's probably going to be a similar story for the RTX 5090, with new units slowing to a trickle as prices continue to rise.

Either way, for most people, the RTX 5090 has been effectively discontinued for months, if not this entire year. It seems like a distant memory at this point, but the RTX 5090 launched in January 2025 for $1,999 , but that price has skyrocketed since. Now that graphics card's price is inching closer to the $10,000 mark, and while there are definitely people who can afford to invest that kind of money into their computer, for most DIY PC gamers, the RTX 5090 might as well not even exist.

If the RTX 5090 was discontinued, it would mostly impact prebuilt gaming PCs. After all, prebuilts strapped with that graphics haven't seen the same astronomical jump in price quite yet, and you can get a decent Alienware tower with a 5090 for less than it costs to just buy the GPU on Newegg right now. But, if Nvidia were to stop manufacturing the RTX 5090, that would likely stop immediately.

It's not clear what's going to happen with the RTX 5090, but regardless, it's hard to imagine any world where the high-end GPU doesn't continue to go up in price as RAMageddon continues. And now that it's rumored that Nvidia won't launch its next-generation graphics cards until 2028 , it could be a long time before any high-end GPU is a reasonable price — if it ever even happens again.

articles.title: Sony Announces $350 All-Black PS5, but You Probably Can't Buy It
articles.summary: After a few price increases, the PS5 will now set you back $599 for the Digital edition, but Sony has just announced a cheaper $350 console – but it's exclusive to Japan.
articles.body:
After a few price increases, the PS5 will now set you back $599 for the digital edition, but Sony has just announced a cheaper $350 console – but it's exclusive to Japan.

In a blog post , Sony announced that it was launching a Japan-only digital 'Midnight Black' PS5 for 55,000 Yen, or approximately $350, on November 19, the same day as Grand Theft Auto 6 . At this point, with hardware prices being what they are, launching an affordable console like this worldwide might genuinely break sales records. However, the console will only be available in Japan.

According to Sony, this model can "only be used with a PlayStation account that has the system language set to 'Japanese' and the 'Country/Region' set to 'Japan.'" While there might be a way to game the system if you're really committed to it, for most people, this version of the PS5 is effectively exclusive to Japanese users.

PlayStation 5 Japan-Exclusive Midnight Black – Photos

This isn't the first time Sony has released a cheaper PS5 for the Japanese market. Back in November 2025, Sony announced a digital PS5 at the same 55,000 Yen price that was similarly exclusive to Japanese users, according to Polygon . However, a lot has changed in the year since then, and it's not just the fancy new colorway.

Pretty much the entirety of 2026 has been marred by price increases at the hands of AI datacenters. This RAMageddon isn't going to let up any time soon , and has already caused Sony to raise the price of the PS5 and PS5 Pro here in the US back in March . And, now that used PS5 Pros are going for around $1,400 , there's likely another price increase around the corner.

So, it's unlikely that Sony is going to announce a similarly-priced PS5 here in the US or in Europe any time soon. However, that 'Midnight Black' colorway doesn't exist here, with the closest version being the Black PS5 sold by Gamestop. But this new, slightly-different colorway is exclusive to Japan, and I'd love to see it released over in the US, even if it carries the same price as any other PS5.

articles.title: Over 1 Million Characters Have Been Made in the WoW Forever Beta
articles.summary: It's no secret that World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular since entering its beta last month, but now, over 1 million characters have been made.
articles.body:
It's no secret that World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular since entering its beta last month, but now, over 1 million characters have been made.

According to classicplus.io, a community website that snapshots data from WoW Forever, 1,003,125 characters have been made in the Classic Plus mode so far. That's a lot, considering that to even make a character you need to have access to the beta, which is primarily done by buying the $60 Skyborne pack.

But even though most people will have to buy access to the Skyborne race to play in the beta, the Skyborne aren't the most popular race on either faction. For both Alliance and Horde players, the fancy blue elves only represent 18.7% of characters created. Instead, for Alliance players, Humans are much more popular at 32.3%, whereas Horde players seem to prefer Undead characters, at 33.5% of the population.

It's important to remember that while 1 million characters might not seem like a lot in a game that had a peak of 12 million players 16 years ago, WoW Forever hasn't even launched yet. The full game doesn't come out until November 4, and anyone playing the beta now only has access to limited parts of the world. At the time of writing, the level cap in the beta is level 30, and characters will be wiped when the full game launches next month.

So, it's impressive that so many people are playing the game right now, knowing that everything they earn in the game is going to vanish in less than a month. It's a good sign for Blizzard, and suggests that when Forever launches, it's going to be incredibly popular, even if it has to go head-to-head with Grand Theft Auto 6, which launches two weeks later — though I imagine there isn't much crossover between the two games.

Even when WoW Forever first entered its beta last month, Blizzard developers were shocked at how popular it was. One developer even said the beta was putting up "the craziest numbers" they'd ever seen. However, Forever hasn't been free of its own controversies. Blizzard has cracked down on players' names, leading some to think they've been unfairly targeted . And, Blizzard is also cracking down on gold selling, leading to WoW streamers getting caught in the crossfire . But, Blizzard has also added the beloved "Kyle's Gone Missing" quest, even though it wasn't added until Burning Crusade, and everybody seems to love that.

articles.title: The X-Files Officially Reopen: Hulu Gives Series Order to Ryan Coogler's Reboot
articles.summary: Ryan Coogler's long-gestating reboot of The X-Files is a go, as Hulu has given the project a full series order.
articles.body:
It's officially time to head down to the FBI's basement and reopen the X-Files. Hulu has given a full series order to Ryan Coogler's reboot of the iconic sci-fi TV series.

The new series is a collaboration between Disney's Onyx Collective, 20th Century Television, and Coogler's Proximity Media. Coogler wrote, directed, and executive produced the pilot. Coogler will executive produce the series alongside Jennifer Yale. Yale will also serve as showrunner. Other executive producers include Proximity Media's Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian and The X-Files creator Chris Carter.

The new series, which is frequently described as a "reboot" or "re-imagining" of the original show, stars Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel as a new pair of intrepid FBI agents investigating cases the Bureau deems especially strange and bizarre. The series' cast also includes Steve Buscemi , Amy Madigan, Ben Foster, Devery Jacobs, Lochlyn Munro, Tantoo Cardinal, Joel D. Montgrand, and Sofia Grace Clifton.

It's unclear whether the new series acts as a sequel to the original or a complete reboot, and whether David Duchovny and Gillian Anderson might reprise their roles as Agents Fox Mulder and Dana Scully, respectively. For their part, both actors have expressed an interest in returning, with Duchovny confirming he's had talks with Coogler .

“I’ve loved ‘The X-Files’ for a long time, so getting the chance to write and direct the pilot has meant a great deal to me,” said Coogler in a statement. “What Chris Carter created is special, and we wanted to honor everything that made the original series connect with so many people while also finding our own way into that world. Danielle and Himesh, along with the rest of our cast, have brought such original perspectives and performances to these characters, and watching that come together has been one of the most rewarding parts of the experience. I couldn’t have asked for better collaborators than my crew, colleagues at Proximity Media and our partners at Onyx Collective and 20th Television. I’m grateful for the trust and support they’ve given us as we take on this new chapter.”

There's no word on a release date for the new X-Files yet. The show's pilot was filmed earlier this year , and presumably production on the rest of Season 1 will begin soon, making a late 2027 release a possibility.

In other The X-Files news, Carter has noted a desire to continue the storyline of the original series , which ended with Season 11 in 2018. Hulu also recently debuted Carter's director's cut of The X-Files: I Want to Believe. Read IGN's review of The X-Files: I Want to Believe - Vrach Frankensteyn .

The franchise is also returning to comics in the near future , with Dynamite Entertainment revealing a new series set during the classic era of the TV show.

Silk & Sorrow can be played in both couch co-op and online co-op, with players needing to communicate, solve problems, and trust one another to survive a world where every step brings new dangers and unsettling discoveries.

articles.title: Nvidia Brings DLSS 5 to Hogwarts Legacy, but Some Fans Can't Tell the Difference
articles.summary: About a month after it debuted in NBA 2K27, DLSS 5 is now being added to Hogwarts Legacy, with a new, faster model.
articles.body:
About a month after it debuted in NBA 2K27, DLSS 5 is now being added to Hogwarts Legacy , with a newer, faster model.

In a blog post, Nvidia announced that it is launching a new model for DLSS 5 that's — according to Team Green — twice as fast as the model that debuted in NBA 2K27 last month . While the basketball game will be getting an update that adds this new model, and thus improves performance, Nvidia is also bringing the neural rendering tech to Hogwarts Legacy and Where Winds Meet in November.

Nvidia has been hard at work getting DLSS 5 to run well enough that people will actually turn it on when they're playing games. It's not hard to see why that's a major focus; when I first tested the tech back in September , I found that it could absolutely cripple my frame rate at 4K on the RTX 5090. It wasn't long ago, either, that Nvidia debuted the technology at GTC 2026 in March , where it needed to run on two RTX 5090s to deliver a playable experience, and even then it was super limited.

Hogwarts Legacy – Nvidia DLSS 5 Screenshots

Now, though, Nvidia claims the new model is twice as fast as September's model, and ten times faster than it was when DLSS 5 was first revealed. If that's true — and I won't know that until I actually test it — it makes sense that developers are now willing to add the feature to their games.

But unlike some of the deep-fried examples I've seen of DLSS getting modded into games, the Hogwarts Legacy examples Nvidia shared in its blog are a lot more subtle. Rather than completely changing the way characters look, like it did when DLSS 5 was first revealed, it mostly just looks like it balances lighting and subsurface scattering.

And I'm not alone there. Over on X/Twitter, NikTek posted a GIF of him scrubbing through an image comparison with DLSS 5 turned on and off, and noted how small of a difference it makes. He then wonders who would actually use it with such a minor visual change and a big performance hit. However, there were some folks who applauded the subtle changes, with jayv7s replying, "This is the correct way to use it, no exaggerated AI slop filters on top, just normal pure improvement."

However, the subtlety of DLSS 5 will ultimately depend on the developer. There are plenty of dials that devs can adjust to make the game look as natural as possible, or leaning in the opposite direction to make games look like some kind of nightmare ripped straight from Midjourney. However, it is at least a little bit reassuring that in NBA 2K27 and now in Hogwarts Legacy, the developers are at least trying to maintain the same aesthetic.

No matter how subtle it is, though, DLSS 5 does work by using AI to re-draw games , even though it is anchored by the geometry and color data provided by the game. That's definitely enough to turn some people off of this tech, but if the changes are subtle enough and the performance continues to improve at this pace, I can see it eventually getting added to more than one or two games.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Carrie-Anne Moss on Her New Series Yaga and That John Wick 'Throwaway Line'
articles.summary: arrie-Anne Moss discusses her new AMC+ thriller Yaga, her lifelong interest in Baba Yaga folklore, and how she really feels about that meta John Wick line.
articles.body:
Carrie-Anne Moss first heard about the new AMC+ drama Yaga at just the right time. The actress, best known for starring in popular blockbuster fare like The Matrix, Star Wars: The Acolyte, and Jessica Jones, says she just happened to be independently researching the mythology behind the Yaga’s plot right before she was brought in.

“I'd actually just been thinking about it, I'd say a week before,” Moss says. “I loved the fact that this had the lore of Baba Yaga. I'm someone who has always been interested in that story. It does work like that a lot for me, where I'll have a thought about something [and] suddenly a script will come across my path that has some kind of connection. I take those kinds of little nods from the ether as serious.”

Yaga, which is debuting an exclusive clip that you can watch in the player above as part of IGN Fan Fest: Fall Edition, offers a modern twist on the classic Baba Yaga myth. Based on the play by Kat Sandler (who serves as showrunner here), the show follows Rapp (Noah Reid), “a private investigator who arrives in the small coastal town of Whittock to investigate the disappearance of a young heir to a powerful fishery, Henry Park (Hudson Williams). He finds himself at odds with an apprehensive local detective, Carson (Clark Backo), a charismatic university professor with a taste for younger men, Katherine (Moss), and a labyrinth of enigmatic suspects, secret lives, and ancient magic.”

Moss, who I spoke to ahead of Yaga’s October 23 premiere, says her interest in the Baba Yaga–a legendary, sinister female monster from Slavic folklore–goes back decades.

“With the lore of Baba Yaga, there's so many different ways that that story has been told,” Moss says. “And our version is inspired by Kat's [play]. I had come across that story when I was in my 20s through a book called Women Who Run With the Wolves. There’s so many ways to tell the story. There's so many different versions of her.”

Fans who watch the show might best know Baba Yaga as the nickname of John Wick, played on screen by Moss’s Matrix costar Keanu Reeves. At one point in Yaga, Moss’s character humorously deadpans “What’s John Wick?” when the franchise is mentioned by another character. Moss says she recognizes fans might consider the line to be a meta joke, but she sees it differently.

“I'm a huge fan of John Wick, so I'll start with that,” Moss says. “And honestly, when I read that line, because it was written a couple of different ways, I'm always hesitant to put a nod towards that kind of thing. And it's not something that I intuitively want to do. It's not my thing. I think I shot it. I said it a couple of different ways, and in the end they choose what they want to put there. So I understand that it's kind of fun. I understand why it was there, and I'm okay with it being in there, but it's a throwaway line.”

Moss says she embraced the unbothered nature of Katherine during production, especially when it came to her on-screen scenes with Heated Rivalry’s Hudson Williams.

“I have some intimate scenes with younger men in this show,” Moss says. “My sons are close in age to Hudson. I mean that's what you do as an actor, right? I mean you're comfortable with that, but at the same time I was respectful of that too. And you feel, I don't know, I don't want to say embarrass[ed] but I could be his mom. And if you have scenes like that, you’re just kind of keeping your own energy, you're keeping your own distance in a way because you don't want to suddenly be their mom, which very easily can happen when you're a nurturing person.”

Moss says that the cast and crew of Yaga filmed the show at a breakneck pace, which she prefers to more drawn-out shoots.

“I think I was there for three weeks,” Moss says. “I have never ever experienced that where it was really fast. Normally when you're shooting something, you'll have a lot of lull time in between takes, which is actually exhausting. On this show, there was no lull. But when there was a hangout, it was definitely fun. I have to say that Noah and Clark were like a little team the whole time and made me laugh so hard. That felt really good. I don't know about you, but when I laugh from my belly, I almost feel like it's a year's worth of therapy.”

Moss, who’s been in some of the biggest franchises of the 21st century, says that while she doesn’t have any particular IP that she likes to nerd out over, she remembers being so caught up in movies as a kid that she would often return to the theater time and time again.

“I was looking at some pictures from when I grew up in the '70s and the '80s,” Moss says. “I went to see movies that I loved as an 11, 12-year-old girl 17 times. Grease. Rocky. Bad News Bears. I probably babysat and saved my money. That was a big part of what I loved to do. I feel that way when I discover a show. My husband and I have this little routine that we do sometimes like, ‘I can't wait ‘til we have dinner and meet me on the couch.’ I love the feeling of ‘I can't wait to see the next episode of a show.’ I do love finding a show and just wanting to watch every episode, and I hope that the people that watch Yaga feel that way.”

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson's War for Roshar Kickstarter Campaign Crosses $1 Million on Its First Day
articles.body:
Brandon Sanderson and Brotherwise Games have officially launched the Kickstarter campaign for War of Roshar , a new strategy board game. Sanderson has been calling this "the big one" in the leadup to this campaign and the fans seem to agree. More than $1 million has already been pledged in the first day, with 23 days left to go.

War for Roshar will join a growing lineup of Cosmere board games in collaboration with Brotherwise. IGN had an exclusive first look at the game earlier this year and loved what we saw. It's a massive tabletop war game that strikes the balance between strategic analysis and abstract gameplay. The theme of the game is rooted deeply in Sanderson's Stormlight Archive series and includes a wealth of art from over 30 different artists.

If you're looking to back this project, there are a number of options available. The featured pledge, called Fifth Ideal, is what will get you pretty much everything. At $295 this tier includes the base game, the Champions Expansion, 3D components, custom card sleeves, and wooden tokens. You'll also get a few different miniatures for the Cosmere RPG, including Mistborn ones from Era 1 and Era 2 to go with the upcoming expansion of that game .

If you don't care about the extra add-ons for the Cosmere RPG , the other four tiers will get you some variation of these items. For just the base game, you can pledge $90 to get access to the retail version as soon as it ships.

As for when the game will actually release, the campaign includes an estimated delivery date of November 2027. This will likely vary depending on where your game is getting shipped to, but Sanderson has a reputation for delivering high-quality products on time for all of his crowdfunding projects.

This is far from the first crowdfunding project that Sanderson has seen enormous success with. Just earlier this year he launched a massive campaign for Hoid's Storybook Collection that ended up raising more than $11 million. IGN's Jordan Comstock went hands-on with those books after they arrived and had no regrets with his choice to back the project.

And prior to that project, Brotherwise game initially funded the Cosmere RPG via kickstarter back in 2024 with a whopping $15 million pledged. So while War for Roshar is off to a great start, we'll have to wait and see if it has the potential to become Sanderson's most successful crowdfunding campaign of all time within his Cosmere universe .

articles.title: Save an Extra 10% Off Alienware's Budget Friendly 27" QD-OLED Gaming Monitor With 240Hz Refresh Rate
articles.summary: Buy two and create a massive 49" 5120x1440 multi-monitor setup for an affordable price.
articles.body:
Most people would agree that OLED monitors are as good as it gets for gaming. They're also really expensive. Well, Alienware is bucking the trend with one of its latest 2026 OLED releases. The 27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD 240Hz QD-OLED gaming monitor is listed at an already reasonable price of $349.99, but right now there's a 10% off discount that drops it to $314.99 with free shipping. It comes with the same three year warranty with OLED burn-in coverage you would get with Alienware's other pricier monitors.

Extra 10% Off 27" Alienware AW2726DM OLED Gaming Monitor

27" Alienware AW2726DM QHD 240Hz QD-OLED Gaming Monitor

The Alienware AW2726DM is a 27" monitor with a 2560x1440 resolution and a pixel density of 111ppi, which is sharp enough for both gaming and general workstation use and boasts excellent text clarity. The panel uses Samsung's quantum dot OLED technology. A QD OLED panel is brighter and has a wider color gamut than the more commonly found W-OLED panel. OLED monitors in general offer superior image quality compared to other monitors thanks to a combination of instantaneous response time, near-infinite black levels, and near-infinite contrast ratio.

Most "budget" OLED monitors have a native 60Hz-144Hz refresh rate, but the AW2726DM ups the ante with a native 240Hz panel, making it a great choice for games that have high-speed motion or require twitch-like reflexes (for example sports games, racing sims, and first person shooters). You'll need to make sure you have an appropriate graphics card to achieve 240fps on a QHD monitor, ideally something like an RTX 5070 Ti or Radeon RX 9070 XT , although an RTX 5070 will be fine for older games like The Witcher 3, Fortnite, Apex Legends, Counter-Strike, or Valorant.

Two of these monitors would make a great multi-monitor setup for the upcoming Forza Horizon 6 game . Two of these monitors side-by-side is equivalent to a 49" monitor with 5120x1440 resolution and it will be a lot cheaper than buying a dedicated 49" OLED monitor with similar specs.

Finally, the AW2726DM does include a 3 year warranty that includes burn-in coverage, which most other brands do not offer. Burn-in is less of an issue than it used to be because there are built-in, automated features designed to prevent it, but it can still happen. Dell offers assurance that it will address the issue if it ever arises.

articles.title: The Best Street Fighter Anime You've Never Seen
articles.summary: The latest Street Fighter movie is hurricane-kicking its way into theaters on October 16 — but did you know there was a critically acclaimed animated film that came out decades before it?
articles.body:
The latest Street Fighter movie is hurricane-kicking its way into theaters on October 16 — but did you know there was a critically acclaimed animated film that came out decades before it?

Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie came out in 1994, the same year that the so-bad-it's-good live-action film with Jean-Claude Van Damme and Raul Julia was released. And while the highly-quotable (“For me, it was Tuesday”) live-action flick is a larger part of the public consciousness, most Street Fighter fans will agree that the animated movie blows it out of the water.

The animated movie doesn’t follow the World Warrior tournament seen in the game; instead, it focuses on Bison tracking down strong warriors using an army of cyborgs in an attempt to capture them for his own nefarious purposes. It’s not an official part of the official Street Fighter lore (which, admittedly, is quite confusing and convoluted), but it features some fantastic fights and, of course, the debut of Violent Ken (an evil version of the character corrupted by M. Bison's Psycho Power).

You’ve likely seen some GIFs from this movie floating around the internet over the years, and that’s no coincidence. The animation in this flick is simply fantastic, especially where fight scenes are concerned. One of the first ones we see takes place between Ryu and Sagat as a little backstory (which actually is canon); other iconic action sequences include Cammy’s assassination of a government official, Ryu and Ken’s final fight against M. Bison, and of course, Chun-Li’s iconic brawl with Vega.

Fights aside, one of the reasons the animated movie is so deeply beloved by fans is that it stays true to Street Fighter’s colorful cast of characters. Just like in the games, Ryu is a deeply contemplative, compassionate man on a perpetual journey of self-improvement; Ken is decidedly more hot-headed but maintains an aura of discipline learned from master Gouken; Guile is a classic American military man whose stoic facade breaks into goofy moments now and then; Chun-Li is a badass kung-fu practitioner who manages to keep hold of her girlish, quirky side; and Bison is a menacing, gangster overlord whose Psycho Power makes him feel like a serious threat.

Given it was the '90s, this version of Street Fighter doesn’t shy away from blood and nudity. In fact, there’s a fairly gratuitous shower scene that highlights Chun-Li’s physique, directly after which she tousles with Vega in a brutal, bloody battle. It’s not a family-friendly film, but it’s possibly the most accurate depiction of what the Street Fighter universe would actually be like if psycho-powered dictators and super-powered martial artists actually roamed the world.

Since it's an animated movie, it's also easier to sell the believability of its overall premise. Live-action adaptations have the challenge of making larger-than-life moves like E. Honda's Sumo Headbutt or Chun-Li's Spinning Bird Kick look realistic enough to fit into the real world; animated movies have the luxury of getting to bypass this, giving artists far more creative freedom in translating these moments from concept to page. This is one of the key reasons why the Street Fighter II animated movie pulls things off so well, and it set the standard for other adaptations in the years to come.

It'd be remiss not to mention the other animated Street Fighter films and series that exist, as well. The Street Fighter Alpha animated movie is a visual spectacle that unfortunately falls flat where story is concerned; the Street Fighter II V anime series is painful to watch, and we won't even get into the mess that was the American cartoon (though it also has some pretty quotable moments). It's clear, though, that the 1994 animated movie is the one to watch out of the lot, and as a diehard Street Fighter fan, I'd argue that it's required viewing if you're trying to get into the franchise.

Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie is available to watch on Crunchyroll, Pluto TV, and Amazon Prime Video at the time of writing this piece. It’s absolutely worth viewing, especially if you’re wanting to learn more about the world of the games ahead of the 2026 movie (or if you just want some badass anime fights). If you’re keen on diving into the games, you can check out our breakdown of how to play each of them in chronological order , or read our article diving into the nearly forty-year-old history of this iconic fighting game franchise from beginning to end.

articles.title: Xbox Announces Xbox Labs, Aimed in Part at Getting Improved Old-Gen Games Playable in Web Browsers
articles.summary: Xbox has announced Xbox Labs, a new initiative aimed at getting games to more people in more places — with a particular emphasis on web browsers.
articles.body:
Xbox has announced Xbox Labs, a new initiative aimed at getting games to more people in more places — with a particular emphasis on web browsers.

No doubt seeing the growing community of games getting improved versions ported into web browsers (like the 94fps browser version of Halo: Combat Evolved), Microsoft itself is keen to get in on the action in support of new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's goal of reaching 1 billion players per day .

Xbox has been tinkering with running Xbox and Xbox 360 games in browsers, and the Xbox Labs initiative is a formalization of those efforts that will see a small team of engineers playing with emerging technologies in order to find new ways for games new and old to be distributed and even created. And IGN understands that this won't just be an R&D effort; rather, Xbox Labs is tasked with shipping products – Sharma says, "We'll build in the open" – and getting gamers to engage with them.

I'd suggest thinking about it as a next phase of the backward compatibility efforts that started at Xbox over a decade ago, which the recent disc-to-digital program built on (which, side note, is a much more consumer-friendly path towards the seemingly inevitable digital future than what Sony is doing ), and now Xbox Labs aims to take it even further. It remains to be seen if or how Xbox will look to monetize its Xbox Labs offerings, be it via an upfront cost, in-game microtransactions, or in-game-ad-based revenue .

The Xbox Labs announcement continues a busy stretch for Xbox, which revealed its entertainment-industry-focused Xbox XP arm last week.

articles.title: Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports
articles.summary: Microsoft has created a new Xbox Labs team to explore game decompiling. It’s an emerging trend that has seen games remixed together.
articles.body: Retro gaming is going through a wild time at the moment, thanks to decompilations and recompilations that are letting gamers port classic titles to new devices, or merge code from two different games into a single new experience. Microsoft has witnessed skateboarding being modded into Call of Duty and Halo being played in a web browser, and the company is now officially embracing the chaos of this new AI-powered era of game modding. Microsoft is putting together a new Xbox Labs group to explore the rapid emergence of these mods, many of which use AI models to help modders remix games in ways we’ve rarely seen before. Xbox Labs will be a “small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience,” says Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. “We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.” Sharma thinks the experiments we’ve seen in recent weeks, where Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside browsers, “challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games.” “While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators,” says Sharma. “These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.“ Modders are now doing the type of work that Microsoft has been doing for decades with its Xbox backward compatibility program, letting old games run on modern hardware. But they’re doing it without the business model restrictions that Microsoft is tied to. It’s starting to feel like we’re just a model or two away from even more breakthroughs that decouple more modern games from their intended hardware. Sharma clearly sees an opportunity here, particularly for AI agent use at Xbox. “I think Xbox has an important role to play here,” says Sharma. “Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide.” Xbox Labs is clearly a way for Microsoft to experiment with how AI will shape where games are played, and Xbox will share any tools and learnings with developers. The bigger question is how Microsoft will respond to decompiles and recompiles of games where modders take its precious IP and make it freely available. Modding is fun, but I can’t see Microsoft and other publishers seeing the fun side if modern console games start to appear where they shouldn’t. I asked Microsoft to comment about unauthorized IP use, but the company didn’t respond in time for publication. Here’s Sharma’s full memo: > Team, > The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we’ve helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together. > In recent weeks, we’ve seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another. > These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models. To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating. > I think XBOX has an important role to play here. Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We’ve spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have. > Our priorities aren’t changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology without abandoning the work already underway. > Asha

articles.title: Officially Licensed Fallout Bookends Are Up for Preorder for a Whopping $325
articles.body:
The Fallout series is one of the most popular video game franchises of all time. Naturally, that means there's a ton of Fallout merch.

Like any product tied to a specific IP, you can always expect some sort of markup on officially licensed products. However, these recently announced Fallout bookends are taking that to a whole new level with a price tag of $325 at Sideshow .

While $325 isn't unheard of for a hand-painted collectible figure, it does seem like an excessive price to pay for a set of bookends. Just to put it in perspective, you can currently get a semi-functional Pip-Boy replica from the IGN Store for only $300. Dark Horse also recently launched, in my opinion, a much cooler set of Fallout bookends for only $179.99 .

So what exactly is making these bookends so expensive? In addition to the licensing fee to collaborate with Bethesda on the product, these bookends apparently weigh four pounds each. They're "meticulously sculpted from polyresin" and individually hand-painted to achieve the antique metal effects the Fallout series is known for.

The official Fallout bookends are available to preorder now with an estimated shipping window of November 2026 - January 2027. According to Sideshow's shipping policy, the company does offer 30 days for returns if you aren't happy with your purchase once you get your hands on it.

Would You Spend $325 for Fallout Bookends?

As someone who has a lot of books and a number of bookends to hold them in place, it seems wild to me that someone would spend this much money for something like this. That being said, I'm not exactly a Fallout superfan with tons of disposable income, so I'm likely not the target market for such a product.

If you're someone who regularly spends a lot of money on collectibles, I'm genuinely curious if this seems like a worthwhile product to drop $350.
